turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
Looking at the training data, the reproducible high‑efficiency recipes share a clear device‑physics signature:

- **HTL is the strongest lever.** PTAA (deep HOMO, low interface recombination, hydrophobic surface giving good MAPbI3 film quality) appears in many of the top rows (17–19%). P3CT‑Na and NiO/NiMg(Li)O are the next best; PEDOT:PSS alone caps lower.
- **ETL:** PCBM‑60 (or C60) plus a thin interlayer (BCP/Bphen/LiF/PEI) that blocks holes and passivates the metal interface is consistently better than bare PCBM. Fullerene‑dye (ITCPTC) / fullerene blends with C60|BCP also reach ~18.5.
- **Contacts:** Ag is the safe baseline; Cu pairs unusually well with PTAA (18.6–18.85); Au pairs well with NiO.
- **Substrate/process:** SLG|ITO or SLG|FTO with spin‑coating (one or two steps) dominates the top; exotic substrates and elaborate multi‑layer electrodes add loss.

Applying this to the pool by closest training analogs:

- **c030** — IDTT2FPDI|PCBM‑60|Bphen / **PTAA|PMMA** / Al: nearly the 19.48 recipe (PCBM|Bphen, PTAA|PMMA, Al); PMMA passivates PTAA interface → top candidate.
- **c044** — PCBM‑60|BCP / **PTAA** / **Cu**: matches the 18.62–18.85 PTAA+Cu family; BCP hole‑blocking + benign Cu contact.
- **c034** — PCBM‑60|C60|BCP / PTAA / Al: direct analog of the 18.85 stack (Al instead of Cu costs a little).
- **c097** — ITCPTC‑Se|C60|BCP / P3CT‑Na / Ag: Se‑analog of the 18.49 ITCPTC‑Th|C60|BCP|P3CT‑Na device; good band cascade and selective contacts.
- **c039** — PCBM‑60|TiO2‑c / NiO‑c / Ag: mirrors the 17.4 ITO and 18.185 FTO/TiO2‑c rows; compact TiO2 improves electron extraction and NiO gives clean hole contact.

Just missing: c007 (PTAA but unproven TrNBr interlayer), c041/c004 (NiMg(Li)O good but FTO+PCBM baseline lower), c064 (PEI instead of BCP weakens blocking).

Final: c030, c044, c034, c097, c039
